Refit a model on new data, with added fixed columns

Source: R/fb_refit.R
fb_refit.Rd

Refits the model of fit on data, with the same random structure, family, priors, engine and engine settings, known variance or covariance, observation weights and offsets. A package built on flexyBayes uses it to refit a user's model on a fold of the data, with candidate columns added to the fixed part, or with brms prior rows and Stan code of its own.

Usage

fb_refit(
  fit,
  data = NULL,
  add_fixed = NULL,
  extra_prior = NULL,
  stanvars = NULL,
  formula_hook = NULL,
  readout = c("full", "varcomp", "fitted", "draws"),
  fixed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

A flexyBayes fit.

data

A data frame with the columns the model uses and any added ones. NULL, the default, refits on the data the fit carries.

add_fixed

Fixed-effect terms to append to the fixed formula: a one-sided formula such as ~ z1 + z2, or a character vector of term labels. NULL adds none.

extra_prior

A brmsprior from brms::set_prior() with rows to add to the prior, or NULL.

stanvars

A stanvars object from brms::stanvar(), or NULL.

formula_hook

A function of formula and prior returning list(formula = , prior = ), or NULL. See "Extending the brms model".

readout

"full", the default, or "varcomp", "fitted" or "draws". See "Readout".

fixed

A two-sided formula that replaces the fit's fixed formula, for a refit whose fixed part differs by more than added terms. NULL, the default, keeps the fit's.

...

Named arguments of flexybayes() that change how this refit runs, for example seed, backend, n_samples, control, na_action, verbose, return_code, weights or known_variance. On the brms route of "Extending the brms model", arguments that flexybayes() does not have go to brms::brm(). Arguments that state the model (random, residual, family, link, known_matrices, prior, prior_fixed_sd, prior_vc_sd) are refused, update() refits a changed model.

Value

A fitted flexyBayes object of the engine the refit ran on, or, with return_code = TRUE, the code that engine would run.

What the refit keeps

  • The fixed formula is the one fit was called with, or fixed, with the terms of add_fixed appended.

  • A prior written with fb_prior(), prior_fixed_sd or prior_vc_sd is passed on as written. The package default prior is built again over the refitted model, as update() does, so on the same data every term keeps the prior it had and an added term gets the default.

  • The engine is the one fit was fitted with, "inla" or "brms", even when the original call asked for "auto". Its recorded sampler settings, seed, control, na_action, fixed_alias and aggregate are passed on.

  • Weights and a known variance belong to rows. A refit on the fit's own data keeps them. A known variance is read from the column of that name in the fit's data, so rows of fit$data carry it. For any other data, pass weights = or known_variance = with one value per row. without them a weighted fit is refused, as is a fit with a known variance whose data lacks the column.

Extending the brms model

extra_prior, stanvars and formula_hook are brms objects, and the refit then runs on brms: fit must be a brms fit, or backend = "brms" must be given. The refit still starts from the brms formula and prior rows the package builds for the model.

formula_hook is called as formula_hook(formula, prior) with that formula and the brmsprior of those rows, and returns list(formula = , prior = ), the formula and prior rows to fit. A non-linear formula usually moves the package's rows onto one of its parts, which is why the hook receives them. extra_prior rows are then merged in, replacing any row with the same class, coef, group, resp, dpar and nlpar, and stanvars is passed to brms::brm(). The fitted object reads under the linear model's names.

Readout

readout names what the caller reads from an INLA refit. "varcomp" (variance components), "fitted" (fitted values) and "draws" (posterior draws, for example on held-out rows) ask INLA for that readout only: no DIC, WAIC or marginal densities, posterior configurations only for "draws", and no second fit to test an AR1 field. The posterior mode, and the readout taken from it, are those of the full refit. A brms refit is always returned in full.

See also

update.flexybayes() to refit with any argument changed.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(site = factor(rep(1:12, each = 10)), x = rnorm(120),
                  z = rnorm(120))
  d$y <- rnorm(12)[d$site] + 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(120)
  fit <- flexybayes(y ~ x, random = ~site, data = d, backend = "inla",
                    verbose = FALSE)
  # The same model with z added, on the first nine sites.
  fold <- fb_refit(fit, data = d[d$site %in% 1:9, ], add_fixed = ~z,
                   verbose = FALSE)
  coef(fold)
}
# }
